items.label: Setup S-1
items.nl: A randomized fixed-horizon trial with a finite baseline alphabet \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\). A full-data law \(P\) is a probability law on the finite record \((X,A,S(0),S(1),Y(0),Y(1),S,Y,R)\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^8\); the observed record is \(O=(X,A,S,R,RY)\), and a sample \(\mathbf O_n=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\) consists of \(n\) i.i.d. copies of \(O\) under \(P\). Cell functionals \(p_{axs}(P)\), \(\rho_{axs}(P)\), \(\mu_{axs}(P)\), \(c_{axs}(P)\) are indexed by \(\mathcal J_d=\{0,1\}\times\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\), the target is \(\tau(P)=E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)]\), estimators \(\mathsf T\in\mathcal T_n\) are all Markov kernels from the finite sample space to \([-1,1]\) that do not depend on \(P\) (deterministic maps are Dirac kernels), and interval procedures \(\mathsf I\) are all such kernels to endpoint pairs \((l,u)\) with \(-1\le l\le u\le1\), with realized interval \([l,u]\); risks, coverage and expected length integrate the sample and the kernel draw jointly. The rare-arrival class \(\mathcal M_{n,d,q}\), the unrestricted-arrival class \(\mathcal M^{+}_{n,d,q}\), and their minimax squared risks and interval-length risks are defined over this world.

items.label: Setup S-2
items.nl: The constructive side of the randomized experiment. With \(N=nq\), \(\ell=\log(e+N)\), \(m=n/6\), \(N_0=mq\), \(k=\lfloor\ell/64\rfloor\) and \(B=256\ell\), a Poisson prefix length \(K_0\sim\operatorname{Poisson}(n/2)\) independent of \(\mathbf O_n\) and a fair three-way stream assignment split the first \(K_0\) records into membership, pilot and estimation streams, producing cell counts \(M_j,C'_j,C_j,U_j\) and statistics \(W_j,D_j,H_j,G_j\). The Chebyshev needle \(Q_k(t)\), built from the first-kind Chebyshev polynomial \(T_k\), has falling-factorial coefficients \(a_v\) used through \((z)_v\); the estimator \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,d,q}\) is the conditional average over the auxiliary randomization of the clipped signed cell sum, \(\mathfrak U_{n,d,q}\) is the explicit deterministic risk envelope, and \(I^{\mathrm{mix}}_\alpha\) is the Markov-inequality interval. The clipped observed-outcome contrast \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HT}}_n=\Pi_{[-1,1]}\{(2/n)\sum_i(2A_i-1)R_iY_i\}\) is used at every arrival floor and is the Horvitz--Thompson arm contrast at complete arrival, where \(\Pi_{[-1,1]}\) is the Euclidean projection onto \([-1,1]\).

items.label: Setup S-3
items.nl: The activated moment-matching lower-bound experiment inside the randomized rare-arrival world. With \(K=\lceil\ell\rceil\), \(H=K^2\), a fixed numerical constant \(\eta\), \(b_0=\eta/(N\ell)\) and \(J=\min\{d-1,\lfloor(2b_0)^{-1}\rfloor\}\), \(J\) rare baseline cells of mass \(b_0\) and one reservoir cell carry latent hardness variables \(Z\) drawn from one of two finitely supported laws \(\Pi_0,\Pi_1\) on \([1,H]\) with matching moments through degree \(K\); a revealed activation flag \(\mathsf B_{\mathrm{act}}\) with parameter-independent law \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(qH)\) yields the pair of fuzzy hypotheses \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{act}}\) whose projection is the original fixed-\(n\) observed experiment.

items.label: Setup S-4
items.nl: The fixed-positivity discrete observational experiment. For \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), a one-record law \(P_Z\) of \((X,B^{\mathrm{obs}},Y)\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\) belongs to \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}\) when every occupied category has propensity in \([\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\); the sample \(\mathbf Z_n\) consists of \(n\) i.i.d. copies, the target is the total functional \(\theta_Z(P_Z)\), \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{poly}}_{n,d,\epsilon}\) is the fair-coin synthetic-assignment average of the mixed-count estimator, and \(\mathfrak R^Z_{n,d,\epsilon}\) is the all-estimator minimax squared risk.

items.label: Definition P-2
items.nl: \(\mathcal E_{n,d,q}:=\{\mathcal L_P(\mathbf O_n):P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,q}\}\), where every record retains \((X,A,S,R,RY)\).

items.label: Definition P-4
items.nl: \(\Phi(P):=2\sum_{(a,x,s)\in\mathcal J_d}g(a)c_{axs}(P)\). When \(P(A=a,X=x,S=s,R=1)>0\), set \(\mu_{axs}(P)=E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x,S=s,R=1]\) and \(c_{axs}(P)=p_{axs}(P)\mu_{axs}(P)\). When the arrived-cell probability is zero, including whenever \(p_{axs}(P)=0\), set \(\mu_{axs}(P)=c_{axs}(P)=0\). Thus \(\Phi\) is total on every full-data law.

items.label: Definition P-6
items.nl:
Let \(\mathcal T_n\) be all parameter-independent Markov kernels from the observed sample \(\mathbf O_n\) to \([-1,1]\), with deterministic estimators included as Dirac kernels. Define
\[
 \mathfrak R_{n,d,q}:=
 \inf_{\mathsf T\in\mathcal T_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,q}}
 \int\!\int_{[-1,1]}(h-\tau(P))^2\,
       \mathsf T(o,dh)\,\mathcal L_P(\mathbf O_n)(do).
\]
Thus \(E_P[(\mathsf T-\tau(P))^2]\) denotes this joint sample-and-kernel risk. By \(\mathrm{lem:randomized\mbox{-}kernel\mbox{-}barycenter}\), the value also equals the deterministic minimax squared risk, while the defining infimum remains over all randomized kernels.

items.label: Definition P-7
items.nl:
Let \(\mathcal C_{n,d,q,\alpha}\) consist of all parameter-independent Markov kernels \(\mathsf I\) from \(\mathbf O_n\) to endpoint pairs \((l,u)\) with \(-1\le l\le u\le1\), satisfying joint sample-and-randomization honesty:
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,q}}
 \int\!\int \mathbf1\{l\le\tau(P)\le u\}\,
       \mathsf I(o,d(l,u))\,\mathcal L_P(\mathbf O_n)(do)
 \ge1-\alpha.
\]
The realized connected interval is \([l,u]\), and define
\[
 \mathfrak L_{n,d,q,\alpha}:=
 \inf_{\mathsf I\in\mathcal C_{n,d,q,\alpha}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,q}}
 \int\!\int(u-l)\,\mathsf I(o,d(l,u))\,
                 \mathcal L_P(\mathbf O_n)(do).
\]
Thus expected length and coverage both integrate the kernel draw. Deterministic connected intervals are included by Dirac kernels; no barycenter reduction is imposed on interval procedures.

items.label: Definition P-8
items.nl:
Draw \(K_0\sim\operatorname{Poisson}(n/2)\) independently of the data and, if \(K_0\le n\), independently assign each of the first \(K_0\) records to the membership, pilot, or estimation stream with probability \(1/3\).  Let \(\omega\) denote this auxiliary randomization.  If \(K_0>n\), set \(\widetilde\tau(\mathbf O_n;\omega)=0\).  Otherwise form \(M_j,C'_j,C_j,U_j,W_j,D_j\) as declared.  If \(N\le1\), set \(\widetilde\tau(\mathbf O_n;\omega)=0\).  If \(N>1\) and either \(\ell<128\) or \(d<\sqrt N\), do not evaluate the Chebyshev quotient or its coefficients and set
\[
 \widetilde\tau(\mathbf O_n;\omega)
 =\operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}\left\{2\sum_{j=(a,x,s)}g(a)W_jD_j\right\}.
\]
Only on the branch \(N>1\), \(\ell\ge128\), and \(d\ge\sqrt N\), form the total quantities \(Q_k,a_v,H_j,G_j\) and set
\[
 \widetilde\tau(\mathbf O_n;\omega)
 =\operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}\left\{2\sum_{j=(a,x,s)}g(a)W_jG_j\right\}.
\]
The named estimator is the sample-measurable conditional average
\[
 \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,d,q}(\mathbf O_n)
 :=E_\omega[\widetilde\tau(\mathbf O_n;\omega)\mid\mathbf O_n].
\]
This is a finite sum over prefix lengths \(K_0\le n\) and their finite stream assignments, plus the known Poisson tail on which the output is zero; hence it is total and deterministic.  The displayed finite expansion defines the auxiliary randomized output, and convexity of squared loss gives the named estimator no larger risk.

items.label: Definition P-9
items.nl:
For integers \(n,d\ge1\) in the rare-arrival slice, let \(K=\lceil\ell\rceil\), \(H=K^2\), for every \(\eta>0\) fixed before \(n,d,q\), put \(b_0=\eta/(N\ell)\), and use \(J=\min\{d-1,\lfloor(2b_0)^{-1}\rfloor\}\) rare baseline cells of mass \(b_0\) plus one reservoir cell. Since \(\ell>1\), one has \(K\ge2\) and \(K\le2\ell\). Call a pair \((\Pi_0,\Pi_1)\) eligible when both are finite probability laws on \([1,H]=[1,K^2]\) satisfying
\[
 \int z^v\,d\Pi_0(z)=\int z^v\,d\Pi_1(z),\qquad 0\le v\le K,
\]
and
\[
 \left|\int z^{-1}\,d\Pi_1(z)-\int z^{-1}\,d\Pi_0(z)\right|\ge\frac1{12}.
\]
The activated handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{act}}\) is defined for every eligible pair. The moment-matched reciprocal-prior lemma ensures that at least one eligible pair exists, and the lower theorem selects one such pair. The rare-arrival slice gives \(qH=qK^2\le4q\ell^2\le1/16\le1\), so \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(qH)\) is valid and \(qZ\le1\) throughout the prior support.

Under either fuzzy hypothesis, draw one \(Z\) from the corresponding \(\Pi_i\) for each rare baseline cell and use that same cell parameter in both arms. Set the retained surrogate coordinate to \(S=0\) deterministically. In every arm and every rare or reservoir cell, independently of \(Z\), reveal \(\mathsf B_{\mathrm{act}}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(qH)\). If \(\mathsf B_{\mathrm{act}}=0\), output \((R,Y)=(0,0)\). Conditional on \(\mathsf B_{\mathrm{act}}=1\), use the following complete rules:
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
 & (R,Y)=(1,1) & (R,Y)=(1,0) & (R,Y)=(0,0)\\ \hline
 \text{treated rare cell} & 1/H & (Z-1)/H & 1-Z/H\\
 \text{control rare cell} & 0 & Z/H & 1-Z/H\\
 \text{reservoir, either arm} & 0 & 1 & 0.
\end{array}
\]
Thus a treated rare cell has projected probabilities \(q,q(Z-1),1-qZ\), arrival probability \(qZ\), and outcome mean \(1/Z\). A control rare cell has projected arrival probability \(qZ\) and \(Y=0\); equivalently, conditional on activation its arrival probability is \(Z/H\). In the reservoir, both arms have projected arrival probability \(qH\) and \(Y=0\); equivalently, arrival is certain conditional on activation. Draw treatment independently with probability \(1/2\), so balanced randomization is retained. Every conditional likelihood factor is a polynomial in \(Z\) of degree at most the activation count. As a finite-cell check, take \(H=4\), \(q\le1/4\), and \(Z\in\{1,4\}\): the flag probability is \(4q\) in every arm and cell, while the treated-rare projection gives respectively \((q,0,1-q)\) and \((q,3q,1-4q)\). If \(J=0\), no rare cell is assigned the nominal mass \(b_0\). If \(J>0\), the floor cap implies \(b_0\le1/2\); in every case \(Jb_0\le1/2\), so the reservoir mass is valid.

items.label: Definition P-10
items.nl: \(I^{\mathrm{mix}}_\alpha=[\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,d,q}-\sqrt{\mathfrak U_{n,d,q}/\alpha},\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,d,q}+\sqrt{\mathfrak U_{n,d,q}/\alpha}]\cap[-1,1]\), where \(\mathfrak U_{n,d,q}\) is the explicit deterministic envelope certified by \(\mathrm{thm:mixed\mbox{-}count\mbox{-}upper}\).

items.label: Definition P-11
items.nl:
\[
\mathcal M^{+}_{n,d,q}:=
\left\{P:\begin{array}{l}
n,d\ge 1,\quad 0<q\le 1,\\
P\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:randomized\mbox{-}independence},
\mathrm{ass:balanced\mbox{-}randomization},
\mathrm{ass:surrogate\mbox{-}consistency},\\
\mathrm{ass:outcome\mbox{-}consistency},
\mathrm{ass:arrival\mbox{-}mar},
\mathrm{ass:occupied\mbox{-}cell\mbox{-}arrival}
\end{array}\right\}.
\]
Thus \(\mathcal M^{+}_{n,d,q}\) imposes no restriction \(q\log^2(e+nq)\le 1/64\); i.i.d. sampling is a property of the experiment and is imposed separately.

items.label: Definition P-12
items.nl:
Fix \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).  Let \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}\) be the set of one-record laws \(P_Z\) of \((X,B^{\mathrm{obs}},Y)\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\) for which, writing
\[
p_x=P_Z(X=x),\qquad
\pi_x=P_Z(B^{\mathrm{obs}}=1\mid X=x),\qquad
\mu_{bx}=E_{P_Z}[Y\mid X=x,B^{\mathrm{obs}}=b]
\]
on every occupied category \(p_x>0\), one has \(\epsilon\le\pi_x\le1-\epsilon\) and \(0\le\mu_{bx}\le1\).  No value of \(\pi_x\) or \(\mu_{bx}\) is required on a category with \(p_x=0\).

items.label: Definition P-13
items.nl:
For \(P_Z\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}\), define the total observed-law functional
\[
\theta_Z(P_Z):=\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_x(\mu_{1x}-\mu_{0x}).
\]
Equivalently, null categories contribute zero.  The statistical theorem below concerns the displayed observed-law functional.

items.label: Definition P-14
Definition P-15
items.nl:
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\mbox{-}sampling}\), let \(\mathcal T_n\) be all parameter-independent Markov kernels from \(\mathbf O_n\) to \([-1,1]\), including deterministic estimators as Dirac kernels. Define
\[
 \mathfrak R^{+}_{n,d,q}:=
 \inf_{\mathsf T\in\mathcal T_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M^{+}_{n,d,q}}
 \int\!\int_{[-1,1]}(h-\tau(P))^2\,
       \mathsf T(o,dh)\,\mathcal L_P(\mathbf O_n)(do).
\]
Here the sample law is the \(n\)-fold i.i.d. observed-data law induced by \(P\), and the procedure kernel is independent of \(P\). Expectations involving \(\mathsf T\) integrate both the sample and the kernel draw. By \(\mathrm{lem:randomized\mbox{-}kernel\mbox{-}barycenter}\), this infimum has the same value as its deterministic counterpart without changing the defining decision class. At \(q=1\) this is the same all-procedure infimum over the complete-arrival subclass; no new decision class is introduced.

items.label: Definition P-16
items.nl:
For every \(n\ge1\), define the total observed-sample map
\[
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HT}}_n(\mathbf O_n)
:=\Pi_{[-1,1]}\!\left\{
\frac{2}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n(2A_i-1)R_iY_i
\right\}.
\]
This same observed-outcome contrast is used at every arrival floor
\(0<q\le1\). On the complete-arrival sample space, where \(R_i=1\) for every
\(i\), its formula is
\[
\Pi_{[-1,1]}\!\left\{
\frac{2}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n(2A_i-1)Y_i
\right\}.
\]
The superscript retains its complete-arrival Horvitz--Thompson interpretation.

items.label: Assumption A-1
items.nl: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed according to the observed-data law induced by \(P\).

items.label: Lemma L-1
items.nl: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,q}\), the ATE is identified by the total observed-cell functional: \[\tau(P)=\Phi(P)=2\sum_{(a,x,s)\in\mathcal J_d}g(a)c_{axs}(P),\] where each null-cell contribution is \(c_{axs}(P)=0\) without assigning \(\mu_{axs}(P)\) on that cell.

items.label: Lemma L-2
items.nl:
For every integer \(K\ge 2\), with \(H=K^2\),
\[
 \inf_{\deg(p)\le K}\sup_{z\in[1,H]}\left|z^{-1}-p(z)\right|
 =\frac{H-1}{2H}\left(\frac{\sqrt H-1}{\sqrt H+1}\right)^K,
\]
where the infimum is over real polynomials.

items.label: Lemma L-3
items.nl:
For every integer \(K\ge2\) and \(H=K^2\), there are finite probability laws \(\Pi_0\) and \(\Pi_1\) on \([1,H]\) such that
\[
 \int z^v\,d\Pi_0(z)=\int z^v\,d\Pi_1(z),\qquad 0\le v\le K,
\]
and
\[
 \left|\int z^{-1}\,d\Pi_1(z)-\int z^{-1}\,d\Pi_0(z)\right|\ge \frac1{12}.
\]

items.label: Lemma L-4
items.nl:
The model contains the single one-cell randomized Bernoulli family \(\{P_u:u\in[1/4,3/4]\}\), chosen independently of \(\alpha\), with \(X=1\), \(S(0)=S(1)=0\), control outcomes zero, balanced randomization, and arrival probability \(q\). There is a universal constant \(\underline c>0\) such that a two-point subfamily gives
\[
 \mathfrak R_{n,d,q}\ge \underline c\min\{1,N^{-1}\}.
\]
For every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), there is a constant \(\underline c_\alpha>0\), independent of \(n,d,q\), and an \(\alpha\)-dependent finite grid selected from this same family such that
\[
 \mathfrak L_{n,d,q,\alpha}\ge \underline c_\alpha\min\{1,N^{-1/2}\}.
\]

items.label: Lemma L-5
items.nl:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M^{+}_{n,d,q}\), the total observed-cell functional identifies the causal target:
\[
\tau(P)=\Phi(P)=2\sum_{(a,x,s)\in\mathcal J_d}g(a)c_{axs}(P).
\]
The equality uses only occupied cells; a null cell contributes \(c_{axs}(P)=0\) and requires no conditional mean.

items.label: Lemma L-6
items.nl:
Fix \(0<q<1/2\).  For every \(P_Z\in\mathcal D_{d,q}\), consider the Markov kernel which, independently for each input record \((x,b,y)\), draws a fair \(u\in\{0,1\}\) and returns
\[
o(x,b,y;u)=\left(x,u,0,\mathbf 1\{b=u\},\mathbf 1\{b=u\}y\right).             \tag{1}
\]
The kernel is independent of \(P_Z\).  For every \(n\ge1\), it maps an i.i.d. sample \(\mathbf Z_n\) from \(P_Z\) to an i.i.d. sample \(\mathbf O_n\) whose one-record law is induced by some \(P_Z^*\in\mathcal M^{+}_{n,d,q}\), and
\[
\tau(P_Z^*)=\theta_Z(P_Z).                                                    \tag{2}
\]

items.label: Lemma L-7
items.nl:
Let \(\mathcal Z\) be a finite sample space, \(\Lambda\) an arbitrary parameter set, \(Q_\lambda\) a probability law on \(\mathcal Z\), and \(\vartheta(\lambda)\in[-1,1]\) a target, for each \(\lambda\in\Lambda\). A randomized estimator is a parameter-independent Markov kernel \(\kappa\) from \(\mathcal Z\) to \([-1,1]\). Define its barycenter by \(b_\kappa(o)=\int h\,\kappa(o,dh)\). For every \(\lambda\),
\[
 \sum_{o\in\mathcal Z}Q_\lambda(o)
       \{b_\kappa(o)-\vartheta(\lambda)\}^2
 \le \sum_{o\in\mathcal Z}Q_\lambda(o)
       \int\{h-\vartheta(\lambda)\}^2\,\kappa(o,dh).
\]
Consequently the minimax squared risk over all such kernels equals the minimax squared risk over all deterministic maps \(b:\mathcal Z\to[-1,1]\), represented by Dirac kernels. The same equality holds if real-valued randomized estimators are allowed on the randomized side: projection onto \([-1,1]\) first reduces every risk. Every bounded scalar kernel can be realized as a measurable map of the sample and a uniform auxiliary seed whose distribution is independent of the parameter.

items.label: Lemma L-8
items.nl:
Let \(Q_0,Q_1\) be probability laws on a finite space \(\mathcal Z\), and let \(\kappa\) be a parameter-independent Markov kernel to any measurable action space \(\mathcal H\). Write \(Q_i\ltimes\kappa\) for the joint input-action law and \(Q_i\kappa\) for its action marginal. With total variation defined as the supremum of absolute probability differences over measurable events,
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_0\kappa,Q_1\kappa)
 \le\operatorname{TV}(Q_0\ltimes\kappa,Q_1\ltimes\kappa)
 =\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1).
\]
In particular, adjoining a common parameter-independent auxiliary seed leaves total variation unchanged, projecting an experiment cannot increase it, and every possibly randomized test satisfies
\[
 \Pr_0\{\psi=1\}+\Pr_1\{\psi=0\}
 \ge1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1).
\]
These conclusions apply to estimator kernels and to connected-interval endpoint kernels, retaining their joint sample-and-randomization laws.

items.label: Theorem T-1
items.nl: There exists a universal \(\overline C<\infty\) such that, for every \(n,d\ge1\), \(0<q\le1\), and \(P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,q}\), \[E_P[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,d,q}-\tau(P))^2]\le\mathfrak U_{n,d,q}\le\overline C r_{n,d,q}.\] The randomized construction is total, and its conditional average over the finite auxiliary randomization is a deterministic estimator with no larger risk.

items.label: Theorem T-2
items.nl:
There exists a universal \(\underline c>0\) such that, throughout \(q\ell^2\le1/64\),
\[
\inf_{\mathsf T\in\mathcal T_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,q}}E_P[(\mathsf T-\tau(P))^2]\ge\underline c r_{n,d,q}.
\]
The comparison is performed in the original fixed-\(n\) experiment \(\mathbf O_n\); it retains every observed \((X,A,S,R,RY)\), uses \(P(A=1)=1/2\), and follows by projecting the parameter-independent activation experiment \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{act}}\), not by discarding memberships or replacing the randomized arms by independent samples. The lower construction has two regimes: a one-cell Bernoulli submodel supplies \(\min\{1,(nq)^{-1}\}\) when \(d\) is small, while the \(J\)-cell activated moment-matching family supplies \(\min\{1,[d/\{nq\log(e+nq)\}]^2\}\) in the many-cell regime; their maximum is equivalent up to universal constants to \(r_{n,d,q}\).

items.label: Theorem T-3
items.nl: There exist universal constants \(0<\underline c\le\overline C<\infty\) such that, for all \(n,d\ge1\) and \(0<q\le1\) satisfying \(q\ell^2\le1/64\), \[\underline c r_{n,d,q}\le\mathfrak R_{n,d,q}\le\overline C r_{n,d,q}.\]

items.label: Theorem T-4
items.nl:
For every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), there exist \(0<\underline c_\alpha\le\overline C_\alpha<\infty\) such that, throughout \(q\ell^2\le1/64\),
\[
\underline c_\alpha\sqrt{r_{n,d,q}}\le\mathfrak L_{n,d,q,\alpha}\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,q}}E_P[\operatorname{length}(I^{\mathrm{mix}}_\alpha)]\le\overline C_\alpha\sqrt{r_{n,d,q}}.
\]
The lower bound ranges over every uniformly honest connected interval and uses a finite family of mutually moment-matched activated priors for arbitrary fixed \(\alpha\).

items.label: Theorem T-5
items.nl: Along every sequence with fixed \(d\), \(N=nq\to\infty\), and \(q\log^2(e+N)\le1/64\), the frontier satisfies \(r_{n,d,q}\asymp N^{-1}\). If \(S(0)=S(1)=0\), the same reduction holds without a surrogate. Thus the proposal reduces to the standard rare-label effective-sample-size order in the fixed-alphabet special case.

items.label: Theorem T-6
items.nl: For sequences in the rare-arrival slice with \(N=nq\to\infty\), uniform consistency is possible if and only if \(d=o\{N\log(e+N)\}\), and the minimax MSE is of order \(N^{-1}\) if and only if \(d=O\{\sqrt N\log(e+N)\}\).

items.label: Theorem T-7
items.nl:
Put \(N_0=mq=N/6\) and \(\gamma_0=\log 2-1/2\).  The following deterministic envelope is finite and depends only on \((n,d,q)\).  If \(N\le1\), set \(\mathfrak U_{n,d,q}=1\).  If \(N>1\) and either \(\ell<128\) or \(d<\sqrt N\), set
\[
 \mathfrak U_{n,d,q}
 =\min\left\{4,
 \left(\frac{8d}{eN_0}\right)^2
 +4\left(\frac4{N_0}+\frac1m\right)
 +4e^{-n\gamma_0}\right\}.
\]
On the remaining branch \(\ell\ge128\) and \(d\ge\sqrt N\), define
\[
 b_{n,d,q}=2\left\{\frac{4dB}{N_0k^2}+3e^{-16\ell}\right\},
\]
\[
 v_{n,d,q}=8\left(\frac4{N_0}+\frac1m\right)
 +64d(e^{\ell/8}+1)
 \left(\frac{B^2}{N_0^2}+\frac{B}{mN_0}\right)
 +32e^{-32\ell}\left(1+\frac1m\right),
\]
and set
\[
 \mathfrak U_{n,d,q}
 =\min\{4,b_{n,d,q}^2+v_{n,d,q}+4e^{-n\gamma_0}\}.
\]
Then, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,q}\),
\[
 E_P[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,d,q}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le \mathfrak U_{n,d,q}\le \overline C r_{n,d,q}
\]
for a universal \(\overline C<\infty\).  In particular, the marked factorial second moment, false-light product, random-membership variance comparison, and capped-prefix transfer introduce no factor depending on \(q\) beyond \(N=nq\).

items.label: Theorem T-8
items.nl:
Put \(N_0=mq=N/6\) and \(\gamma_0=\log 2-1/2\).  Define a deterministic envelope as follows.  If \(N\le1\), set \(\mathfrak U_{n,d,q}=1\).  If \(N>1\) and either \(\ell<128\) or \(d<\sqrt N\), set
\[
\mathfrak U_{n,d,q}
=\min\left\{4,
\left(\frac{8d}{eN_0}\right)^2
+4\left(\frac4{N_0}+\frac1m\right)
+4e^{-n\gamma_0}\right\}.
\]
If \(N>1\), \(\ell\ge128\), and \(d\ge\sqrt N\), put
\[
b_{n,d,q}=2\left\{\frac{4dB}{N_0k^2}+3e^{-16\ell}\right\},
\]
\[
v_{n,d,q}=8\left(\frac4{N_0}+\frac1m\right)
+64d(e^{\ell/8}+1)
\left(\frac{B^2}{N_0^2}+\frac{B}{mN_0}\right)
+32e^{-32\ell}\left(1+\frac1m\right),
\]
and
\[
\mathfrak U_{n,d,q}
=\min\{4,b_{n,d,q}^2+v_{n,d,q}+4e^{-n\gamma_0}\}.
\]
Then, under i.i.d. sampling, for every \(n,d\ge1\), every \(0<q\le1\), and every \(P\in\mathcal M^{+}_{n,d,q}\),
\[
E_P[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,d,q}-\Phi(P))^2]
\le \mathfrak U_{n,d,q}\le \overline C r_{n,d,q}
\]
for a universal \(\overline C<\infty\).  No rare-arrival-slice condition is used.

items.label: Theorem T-9
items.nl:
There exists a universal \(\overline C<\infty\) such that, under i.i.d. sampling, for every \(n,d\ge1\), \(0<q\le1\), and \(P\in\mathcal M^{+}_{n,d,q}\),
\[
E_P[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,d,q}-\tau(P))^2]
\le\mathfrak U_{n,d,q}\le\overline C r_{n,d,q}.
\]
The conditional average over the finite auxiliary randomization is a total deterministic estimator with no larger risk.

items.label: Theorem T-10
Theorem T-11
Theorem T-12
items.nl:
For every fixed \(0<q<1/2\), along sequences with \(n\to\infty\) and possibly varying integer \(d\ge1\), the unrestricted-arrival point-risk frontier obeys
\[
\mathfrak R^{+}_{n,d,q}\to0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
d=o\{n\log(e+n)\}.                                             \tag{1}
\]
The parametric regime has the following explicit uniformity. There is \(c(q)>0\), depending only on the fixed \(q\), such that for every \(M>0\) there are \(C(q,M)<\infty\) and \(n_0(q,M)<\infty\) for which
\[
 \frac{c(q)}n\le \mathfrak R^{+}_{n,d,q}\le\frac{C(q,M)}n       \tag{2}
\]
for every \(n\ge n_0(q,M)\) and every integer \(1\le d\le M\sqrt n\log(e+n)\). Conversely, for any particular integer sequence \(d_n\ge1\), if there are constants \(0<c_*\le C_*<\infty\) and \(n_*<\infty\), allowed to depend on \(q\) and on that sequence, such that
\[
 \frac{c_*}n\le \mathfrak R^{+}_{n,d_n,q}\le\frac{C_*}n
 \qquad(n\ge n_*),                                           \tag{3}
\]
then there are \(M_*<\infty\) and \(n_1<\infty\) with
\[
 1\le d_n\le M_*\sqrt n\log(e+n)\qquad(n\ge n_1).            \tag{4}
\]
Thus, for each fixed dimension sequence, parametric order is equivalent to \(d_n=O\{\sqrt n\log(e+n)\}\), with the upper comparison constant allowed to depend on its fixed growth bound. These are point-risk conclusions only; they do not extend the connected-interval frontier beyond the rare-arrival slice.

items.label: Theorem T-13
items.nl:
Under i.i.d. sampling, for every \(n,d\ge1\),
\[
\frac{1}{256n}
\le \mathfrak R^{+}_{n,d,1}
\le
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M^{+}_{n,d,1}}
E_P\!\left[
\left\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HT}}_n-\tau(P)\right\}^2
\right]
\le \frac{4}{n}.                                           \tag{1}
\]
Consequently \(\mathfrak R^{+}_{n,d,1}\asymp n^{-1}\) with
universal constants, uniformly over the baseline alphabet size \(d\).
This is a point-risk assertion at the complete-arrival endpoint
\(q=1\); it asserts neither the same order for any \(q<1\) nor an
unrestricted connected-interval result.

items.label: Theorem T-14
items.nl:
For every sequence \(n\to\infty\) and every possibly \(n\)-dependent
alphabet size \(d\ge1\),
\[
\mathfrak R^{+}_{n,d,1}\asymp n^{-1},                       \tag{1}
\]
with comparison constants independent of the chosen alphabet sizes.
Thus the complete-arrival endpoint has no dimension-growth elbow for
point risk: arbitrary growth of \(d\) retains parametric order.  The
statement is confined to \(q=1\) and does not concern unrestricted
connected intervals.

items.label: Theorem T-15
items.nl:
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\mbox{-}sampling}\), there is a universal
\(\overline C<\infty\), which may be chosen as in
\(\mathrm{thm:unrestricted\mbox{-}mixed\mbox{-}count\mbox{-}upper}\), such that for every
\(n,d\ge1\) and \(0<q\le1\),
\[
\frac{1}{256n}\le\mathfrak R^{+}_{n,d,q}
\le\min\left\{1,\overline C r_{n,d,q},\frac4n+(1-q)^2\right\}.
\]
The already-defined clipped observed-outcome contrast satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M^{+}_{n,d,q}}
E_P\!\left[\left\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HT}}_n-\tau(P)\right\}^2\right]
\le\frac4n+(1-q)^2.
\]
The minimax infimum is over every parameter-independent bounded estimator
kernel in \(\mathrm{def:unrestricted\mbox{-}minimax\mbox{-}risk}\).
No rare-arrival-slice condition is imposed. This theorem concerns point risk.

items.label: Theorem T-16
items.nl:
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\mbox{-}sampling}\), let \(n\to\infty\), let
\(d_n\ge1\) be arbitrary integers, and let \(q_n\in(0,1]\).
Fix a finite constant \(M\ge0\). If \(1-q_n\le M/\sqrt n\) eventually, then
\[
\frac1{256n}\le\mathfrak R^{+}_{n,d_n,q_n}
\le\frac{4+M^2}{n}
\qquad\text{eventually}.
\]
Thus \(\mathfrak R^{+}_{n,d_n,q_n}\asymp n^{-1}\), uniformly over arbitrary
alphabet growth, with the upper comparison constant depending only on
\(M\). This is a sufficient dimension-free near-complete-arrival window;
no necessity statement or unrestricted connected-interval conclusion is
asserted.

items.label: Theorem T-17
items.nl:
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\mbox{-}sampling}\), for every integer
\(n\ge1\), integer \(d\ge1024n^2\), and \(0<q\le1\), the unrestricted
all-kernel point risk satisfies
\[
\max\left\{\frac1{256n},\frac{(1-q)^2}{1024}\right\}
\le\mathfrak R^{+}_{n,d,q}
\le\frac4n+(1-q)^2.
\]
In particular,
\[
\frac1{2048}\left\{\frac1n+(1-q)^2\right\}
\le\mathfrak R^{+}_{n,d,q}
\le4\left\{\frac1n+(1-q)^2\right\}.
\]
All constants are universal. The lower bound applies directly to every
parameter-independent bounded estimator kernel in
\(\mathrm{def:unrestricted\mbox{-}minimax\mbox{-}risk}\), while retaining the
full observations and fair randomized treatment. No rare-arrival-slice
condition or connected-interval assertion is imposed.

items.label: Theorem T-18
items.nl:
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\mbox{-}sampling}\), let
\((q_n)_{n\ge1}\) be any sequence in \((0,1]\). Then
\[
\frac1{2048}\{1+n(1-q_n)^2\}
\le\sup_{d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge1}n\mathfrak R^{+}_{n,d,q_n}
\le4+n(1-q_n)^2
\qquad(n\ge1).
\]
Consequently the following conditions are equivalent:
\[
1-q_n=O(n^{-1/2}),
\]
\[
\text{there exist }D<\infty\text{ and }n_*\in\mathbb N
\text{ such that }
\mathfrak R^{+}_{n,d,q_n}\le D/n
\text{ for every }n\ge n_*\text{ and every integer }d\ge1.
\]
The universal lower bound \(\mathfrak R^{+}_{n,d,q_n}\ge1/(256n)\)
then supplies matching parametric order for every alphabet sequence.
If \(\sqrt n(1-q_n)\) is unbounded, the allowed sequence
\(d_n=1024n^2\) satisfies
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}n\mathfrak R^{+}_{n,d_n,q_n}=\infty.
\]
Necessity is for a guarantee uniform over arbitrary alphabet growth;
no necessity statement for each fixed alphabet sequence and no
unrestricted connected-interval result is asserted.

items.label: Cited result lem:zeng-theorem-two-lower
items.nl:
Fix \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).  There exist constants \(c_\epsilon>0\), \(c_0>0\), and \(n_0<\infty\) such that, whenever \(n\ge n_0\) and \(1\le d\le c_0n\log n\),
\[
\inf_{\widehat\theta}
\sup_{\substack{P_Z\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}:\\ \mu_{0x}=0\text{ on occupied }x}}
E_{P_Z}\!\left[(\widehat\theta-\theta_Z(P_Z))^2\right]
\ge c_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\left(\frac d{n\log n}\right)^2\right\}.
\]
The infimum is over all estimators based on the i.i.d. observational sample.
